newsitem.title: USA: AgroEvo developments seen adding $2 bln to sales.
newsitem.headline: AgroEvo developments seen adding $2 bln to sales.

text.p: AgroEvo projects now in the development pipeline will be producing annual sales of $2 billion in six to eight years, North American chief executive Maurice A. Delage told reporters.
Speaking at Hoechst AG first Research & Development Day, he said $700 million of those sales by year 2002 will come from the company Liberty Link herbicide project.
AgroEvo is expected to have sales of $3.6 billion this year, Delage said.

He noted that includes the Dutch/Belgian biotech research company Plant Genetic Systems International AgroEvo acquired in August. The company is 60 percent owned by Hoechst and 40 percent by Schering AG.
Based on 1995 sales of $2.36 billion, AgrEvo is the second largest crop production company in the world, Chief Executive Officer Gerhard Prante told security analysts in a separate presentation.
This was well behind Novartis, which is being formed by a merger of Swiss-based Ciba-Geigy AG and Sandoz AG SANZ.Z.
Prante put its combined sales in this area at $4.37 billion and said AgroEvo was followed closely by Monsanto Co, Bayer AG and DuPont Co.

Hoechst and AgroEvo declined to provide specifics on Liberty Link's development costs, although Utz-Hellmuth Flecjht, the Hoechst Board of Management member responsible for research said, "you are talking definately three-digit million (dollar) numbers."
Delage said Liberty Link, which is now in the launch phase, has taken 10 years to develop.
The Liberty Link system combines a broad-spectrum, one-shot, post-emergence herbicide with seeds for plants that have been genetically altered to tolerate the herbicide.
He said there has been capital spending "in the range of $100 million" to develop production facilities for the Liberty herbicide.
Delage said the payback for agriculture products developed with biotechnology is "much faster" than for traditional chemistry, but provided no specifics.

He said seeds for Liberty herbicide tolerant Canola seeds were introduced in Canada last year. Liberty Link corn is expected to be launched in the U.S. next year and in Europe in 1998, the same year soybeans will be available in the U.S.
These plants will be followed by sugarbeets in the U.S. and Europe in 199, cotton in 2000 and rice in the U.S. in 2001. -- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.
